articles.title: The Banff Patellofemoral Instability Instrument 2.0 : structural validity and responsiveness as a patient-centred tool for assessing recovery after medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction.
articles.authors: Sze IN, Kerslake S, Hiemstra LA
articles.study_type: Validation study of a patient-reported outcome measurement tool
articles.population: Patients undergoing medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Structural validity, internal consistency, construct validity, floor and ceiling effects, and responsiveness of the Banff Patellofemoral Instability Instrument 2.0 across five domains measured at baseline, 6, 12, and 24 months after surgery
articles.take_home: The Banff Patellofemoral Instability Instrument 2.0 is a reliable questionnaire for measuring how well patients recover after kneecap ligament surgery, with most improvement happening in the first six months and continued gradual improvement up to two years.

articles.title: After-hours hip fracture surgery-influence on reoperation risk, mortality, and surgical complications: a cohort study of 98,607 patients from the Norwegian Hip Fracture Register.
articles.authors: Boutera AT, Dybvik E, Engesaeter LB, Guy P, Kristensen TB, Leer-Salvesen S, et al.
articles.study_type: Cohort study using national registry data
articles.population: Patients aged 65 years and older with hip fracture
articles.outcomes: 1-year reoperation risk, 30-day mortality, and intraoperative complications, stratified by time of surgery (daytime, evening, nighttime)
articles.take_home: Hip fracture surgery performed in the evening or at night was not associated with worse outcomes than daytime surgery. Nighttime surgery was even associated with slightly lower 30-day mortality rates.

articles.title: Extensor Mechanism Allograft After Total Knee Arthroplasty: An Effective Procedure With a Major Risk of Complications.
articles.authors: Ecki M, Deroche E, Servien E, Lustig S, Batailler C
articles.population: Patients who underwent extensor mechanism allograft after total knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 51 knees from 60 procedures performed between 2017 and 2022
articles.outcomes: Allograft survival rates, functional outcomes, complications and reoperations. Mean active extension deficit 22.0 degrees. Kaplan-Meier survival without failure at 24 months was 79.5% and at 48 months was 59.1%. 29.4% experienced complications with 17.6% requiring surgical reoperation.
articles.take_home: Extensor mechanism allograft is an effective salvage procedure for a rare knee complication, but just over half of patients were satisfied with results and complication rates are substantial. About one in six patients needed further surgery to address failure of the graft.

articles.title: Total Joint Arthroplasty Yields Comparable Functional Gains Across the Body Mass Index Spectrum.
articles.authors: Singh M, Scannell DE, Sai S, Park JJ, Wang AL, Harary J, et al.
articles.population: Adults undergoing total hip or knee replacement between 2018 and 2024
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcome measures including PROMIS (Overall, Physical, Mental) and disease-specific scores (HOOS Jr for hip, KOOS Jr for knee) at one year
articles.take_home: Higher body mass index was not independently associated with worse outcomes after hip or knee replacement surgery. Despite starting with worse function, patients with higher BMI achieved substantial improvements comparable to those with lower BMI.

articles.title: Outcomes of Rotating Hinge Knee Implants in Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty: Instability as a Potential Risk Factor for Mechanical Failure.
articles.authors: Vincent A, Servien E, Lustig S, Batailler C
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision total knee arthroplasty with rotating hinged knee implants
articles.outcomes: Implant survival rates, complications (aseptic loosening, dislocation, extensor mechanism rupture), and revision rates at minimum two years follow-up
articles.take_home: Rotating hinged knee implants in revision knee replacement surgery had acceptable survival rates of 79% at five years, but patients who had the surgery for instability were at significantly higher risk of needing further revision. The implants carry a notable complication rate, with loosening, dislocation and tendon rupture occurring in a small but meaningful proportion of patients.

articles.title: Detrimental Mental Health Outcomes Following Periprosthetic Joint Infection: A Systematic Literature Review.
articles.authors: Shehadeh TH, Lizcano JD, Villa JM, Mont MA, Higuera-Rueda CA
articles.population: Patients undergoing treatment for periprosthetic joint infection following total joint arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Mental health outcomes including depression, anxiety, and quality-of-life measures; prevalence of depression 27.3-36.1%, anxiety up to 29.8%
articles.take_home: Patients treated for joint infections after hip or knee replacements experience significantly worse mental health outcomes, including depression and anxiety, compared to those having standard operations, and these psychological effects often persist even after successful treatment.

articles.title: Effect of Excision of the Infrapatellar Fat Pad in Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Double-Blinded Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Howard A, Naeem H, Wood A, Santini A, Davidson J, Phillipson A, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing elective primary total knee replacement for osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS) at 24 months (primary); Oxford Knee Score at 3, 12 and 24 months (secondary)
articles.take_home: Whether the infrapatellar fat pad was removed or kept during knee replacement made no meaningful difference to pain or function at two years. Both groups improved significantly, suggesting the choice of whether to remove this tissue during surgery does not affect patient outcomes.

articles.title: Reverse Reconstruction of the Patient-Specific Anatomy of the Knee: Deep Learning-Based Point Cloud Completion Model.
articles.authors: Kong L, Liu J, Kang H, Xu C, Song H, Wang F
articles.study_type: Validation study of a deep learning algorithm
articles.population: Virtual testing on 140 normal knees from CT scans; preliminary clinical testing in patients with unilateral post-traumatic osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 140 knees in virtual testing; number of clinical patients not specified
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of reconstructing missing knee bone structure using deep learning, measured by geometric distance and anatomical parameter consistency
articles.take_home: A deep learning method called CRA-PCN can accurately reconstruct missing or damaged knee bone structures to within about 1.2 millimetres of the normal knee, potentially helping surgeons plan personalised knee replacements and understand osteoarthritis. However, larger clinical studies are needed before this can be used in routine practice.

articles.title: Defining the terminology of hip and groin pain in 2026: A scoping review of consensus statements.
articles.authors: Becker N, Papadopoulou T, Ahmad SS, Ayeni OR, Beaufils P, Holmich P, et al.
articles.population: Young and middle-aged active individuals with hip and groin pain
articles.outcomes: Terminology and classification systems for hip and groin pain; citation impact of consensus statements; clinical adoption of proposed terminology
articles.take_home: Multiple different naming systems exist for groin pain, but doctors agree more on how to classify hip joint pain. The Doha agreement terminology is most commonly used by clinicians, but better agreement across all hip and groin pain conditions is needed for consistent treatment and research.

articles.title: Bone marrow stimulation improves 12-month clinical outcomes after isolated meniscal repair: A double-blind randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Pakmanee N, Limitlaohaphan C, Saengpetch N, Kijkunasathian C, Lertbutsayanukul C, Wanitchanont T, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 18-60 years with isolated meniscal tears
articles.outcomes: International Knee Documentation Committee score, WOMAC score, Lysholm score, Tegner activity scale, pain, patient satisfaction, meniscal healing on MRI at 12 months
articles.take_home: Adding bone marrow stimulation to standard meniscal repair surgery led to better pain relief, function and patient satisfaction at 12 months compared to standard repair alone. Both approaches resulted in similar healing on imaging scans, with no additional complications from the extra treatment.

articles.title: Time-loss burden and diagnostic-label capture of hip and groin injuries in elite men's football: An 18-season cohort of five major European leagues.
articles.authors: Martins EC, Gomes DA, de Campos Gurgel HM, Chahla J, Murata Y, Ayeni O, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort analysis of publicly reported injury data
articles.population: Elite men's football players across five major European leagues (Premier League, LaLiga, Serie A, Bundesliga, Ligue 1)
articles.sample_size: 50,723 player-seasons; 2,678 publicly reported hip and groin injuries in 1,836 players over 18 seasons (2007/08 to 2024/25)
articles.outcomes: Frequency and time-loss burden of hip and groin injuries; days and matches missed; severity; concentration of burden across injury labels and individual players; capture rate of specific hip-preservation diagnoses in public databases
articles.take_home: Adductor injuries were the most common hip and groin injury in elite football, but pubic-related injuries caused longer absences from play. Time lost from injury was concentrated in a small number of players, with the top 5.4% of affected players accounting for over a quarter of all days missed.

articles.title: Bone graft type is the key determinant of resorption after arthroscopic iliac crest bone grafting: A multicenter study.
articles.authors: Boehm E, Brune D, Lazaridou A, Schoemig F, Hachem AI, Scheibel M
articles.population: Patients undergoing arthroscopic iliac crest bone grafting for anterior shoulder instability with glenoid bone loss
articles.outcomes: Graft resorption measured as percentage loss of glenoid surface area between postoperative and minimum 1-year follow-up CT scans
articles.take_home: Allograft bone lost significantly more material over time than autograft bone after shoulder surgery, with allografts showing about 8 percentage points more resorption. Other factors like how the graft was fixed or positioned did not affect how much bone was lost.

articles.title: Coronal Plane Alignment of the Knee Type I knees are not a homogeneous phenotype : differences in coronal alignment sensitivity following total knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Kawaguchi K, Yamagami R, Kono K, Young SW, Tay ML, Taketomi S, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty with CPAK Type I knee alignment
articles.outcomes: Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS) at one year; associations between coronal alignment changes and clinical outcomes
articles.take_home: CPAK Type I knees are not all the same, and mild varus knees (Type Ia) have worse outcomes when the joint line position changes significantly from its natural position after surgery, whilst severe varus knees (Type 0) are less sensitive to these changes. This suggests surgery may need to be personalised based on how severe the initial deformity is.

articles.title: New Large Language Models Outperform Older Models and Hallucinate Less in Operative Note Data Extraction.
articles.authors: Mulford KL, Yang L, Williams DW, Khosravi A, Le M, Ulrich MN, et al.
articles.study_type: Comparative evaluation of large language models
articles.population: Total hip arthroplasty operative notes
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of data extraction for surgical approach, fixation technique and bearing surface; hallucination rates for each variable
articles.take_home: A newer large language model extracted hip replacement surgery details more accurately than an older model and made up information far less often, though some hallucinations still occurred. The newer model also required simpler instructions to achieve better results.

articles.title: A Systematic Review of Skin Substitutes and Collagen Dressings for Primary Surgical Wound Healing: Implications for Total Joint Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Cochrane NH, Padgett BM, Fillingham YA, Hannon CP
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total joint arthroplasty or any surgical procedure with primary wound closure
articles.outcomes: Wound complication rates, wound healing time, wound-related reoperations
articles.take_home: There is not enough good quality evidence to recommend using skin substitutes or collagen dressings routinely after hip or knee replacement surgery, even though some studies in other types of surgery showed modest benefits in wound healing.

articles.title: Patient Profile and Cause-Specific Lifetime Revision Risk of Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty: An Australian Orthopaedic Association National Joint Replacement Registry Study.
articles.authors: Rele S, Zhou Y, MBiostat CH, Smith PN, Stevens JM
articles.study_type: Registry analysis of primary total knee arthroplasty outcomes
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty for osteoarthritis in Australia between 2000 and 2020
articles.outcomes: Cumulative lifetime revision risk stratified by age, sex, body mass index, American Society of Anesthesiology score, and cause of revision
articles.take_home: Younger patients, particularly men aged 46 to 50 years, have the highest lifetime risk of needing revision surgery after knee replacement, with this risk decreasing substantially with increasing age. Infection was the leading cause of revision across all ages.

articles.title: Effect of Prosthesis Selection on Gap Balancing in Robotic-Assisted Cruciate-Retaining and Posterior-Stabilized Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Yang C, Zhu K, Dai H, Yang D, Zhang X, Chen D, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing robotic-assisted total knee replacement
articles.outcomes: Flexion-extension gaps, bone resection amount, femoral component rotation, alignment, and postoperative knee function scores at 2-year follow-up
articles.take_home: Both types of robotic-assisted knee replacement performed similarly in terms of clinical outcomes at 2 years, though the cruciate-retaining design showed better gap balance and the posterior-stabilised design required less bone removal. The choice between designs should be based on the patient's ligament status and gap balance rather than expected functional differences.

articles.title: Survivorship of Second-Generation Titanium Metaphyseal Cones in Aseptic Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty: Outcomes at a Mean 5.8-Year Follow-up.
articles.authors: Malkani AL, Soderstrom J, Mashni SJ, Duffy RR, Mouzaheim H, Smith LS
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision knee replacement for aseptic bone loss
articles.sample_size: 117 patients with 106 tibial and 34 femoral titanium cones
articles.outcomes: Implant survivorship, revision surgery rates, complications including infection and loosening
articles.take_home: Titanium cone implants used to treat bone loss during revision knee replacement showed good survival rates of 93-96% at seven years. The main reasons for failure were infection and loosening of components that did not use cones, rather than problems with the cones themselves.

articles.title: The Triple-Tapered Uncemented Femoral Stems in Slight Varus Demonstrated Excellent Early Survivorship and Clinical Results.
articles.authors: Kelley BE, Ji B, Bedard NA, Taunton MJ, Pagnano MW, Abdel MP, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective review of institutional joint registry
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty with triple-tapered uncemented femoral stems
articles.outcomes: Femoral stem revision rates, periprosthetic fracture rates, Harris Hip Scores, and radiographic findings at mean two-year follow-up (range 2 to 8 years)
articles.take_home: Triple-tapered femoral stems positioned in slight varus alignment showed excellent survival rates and did not increase fracture risk compared to neutral alignment. This finding suggests that varus positioning from standard surgical techniques does not harm the long-term stability of these implants.

articles.title: Computer-Assisted Navigation Combined with Three-Dimensional-Printing Custom Augments for Personalized Bone Defect Restoration and Acetabular Reconstruction in Complex and Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Zheng Y, Geng X, Zhang Y, Li Z, Li F, Zhao M, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing complex primary or revision total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of acetabular angle positioning, leg length difference, Harris Hip Score, WOMAC score, SF-12 score, and perioperative complications
articles.take_home: A navigation system using CT imaging and 3D printing custom implants helped surgeons accurately position hip replacement components in complex cases, with patients showing improved function after surgery and minimal complications.

articles.title: Association of Cutaneous Keloids and Hypertrophic Scarring with Risk of Postoperative Arthrofibrosis After Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Williams S, Ceballos-Alvarez KE, Mao E, Thakkar S
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national database
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty, with and without history of cutaneous keloids or hypertrophic scarring
articles.sample_size: 12,610 patients (6,305 per matched cohort after propensity score matching)
articles.outcomes: Arthrofibrosis, revision knee replacement, manipulation under anesthesia, and periprosthetic joint infection at 30 days, 60 days, one year, and two years postoperatively
articles.take_home: Patients with a history of keloids or hypertrophic scarring had significantly higher rates of arthrofibrosis (stiffness), need for revision surgery, and infection after knee replacement compared to those without this history. This scarring tendency may help identify patients at higher risk of complications after knee replacement.

articles.title: A randomized study on migration of the Spectron EF and the Charnley flanged 40 cemented femoral stems: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial using radiostereometric analysis (RSA) with 10 years' follow-up.
articles.authors: Johannessen HG, Hallan G, Furnes O, Fenstad AM, Lygre SH, Haugan K, et al.
articles.study_type: Randomised controlled trial with radiostereometric analysis
articles.population: Patients undergoing cemented total hip replacement (mean age 70 years, 70% women)
articles.sample_size: 150 patients randomised; 48 patients (14 Charnley, 34 Spectron EF) with evaluable data at 10 years
articles.outcomes: Stem migration (retroversion, subsidence, posterior translation) measured by radiostereometric analysis; Harris Hip Score for clinical outcomes
articles.take_home: After 10 years, the Spectron EF stem showed less retroversion but slightly more subsidence than the Charnley stem, with both stems achieving similar good clinical outcomes. Spectron EF stems with highly crosslinked polyethylene had more subsidence than those with conventional polyethylene.

articles.title: The impact of functional sagittal pelvic tilt on CT-based hip dysplasia diagnostics in adults: a cross-sectional 3D simulation study.
articles.authors: Husken MFT, Lissendorp F, Magre J, Willemsen K, Weinans H, Sakkers R, et al.
articles.population: Adults with hip dysplasia
articles.outcomes: Changes in acetabular measurements (LCEA, AI, AASA, PASA, HASA, AV, EI, total coverage, loadbearing coverage) across different pelvic tilt positions
articles.take_home: When pelvic tilt was simulated from lying flat to standing positions, most CT measurements of hip dysplasia changed only slightly, though some measurements like anterior acetabular angle and acetabular version changed by around 4 degrees, which could matter in borderline cases.

articles.title: Prevention of Venous Thromboembolism after Total Hip or Knee Replacement.
articles.authors: Pellegrini VD Jr, Lambourne CA, Magder LS, Franklin PD, Magaziner JS, Martin BI, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing elective total hip or knee replacement
articles.outcomes: Death from any cause or symptomatic blood clots within 6 months; bleeding, reoperation for wound problems, or heart attack within 6 months
articles.take_home: Aspirin was less effective than rivaroxaban or warfarin at preventing death or blood clots after hip or knee replacement. Warfarin and rivaroxaban caused more bleeding and other safety issues than aspirin, so there is no clear winner between all three drugs.

articles.title: The Rapid Rise of Cementless Total Knee Arthroplasty in Canada.
articles.authors: Laende EK, Loughlin N
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national registry data
articles.population: Adults aged 18 years and over undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty in Canada
articles.outcomes: Proportion of cementless versus cemented fixation; variation by patient sex, age, and province; implant model distribution
articles.take_home: The use of cementless knee replacements in Canada more than doubled between 2019 and 2023, rising from 8.4% to 18.6% of procedures. Younger patients and men were more likely to receive cementless implants, though most of this increase was driven by uptake of a single implant system.

articles.title: Patient-Reported Outcomes Differ Across Five Contemporary Alignment, Implant and Technology Pathways in Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Lum ZC, Tse S, Lee P, Giordani M, Meehan JP
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty at a single institution
articles.sample_size: 1,239 total knee arthroplasties across five technique pathways
articles.outcomes: One-year patient-reported outcome measures including Forgotten Joint Score-12 (FJS-12), Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score for Joint Replacement (KOOS JR), PROMIS Global Health, Veterans RAND-12, expectation fulfillment and patient-acceptable symptom state
articles.take_home: Robotic restricted kinematic alignment produced better results on the joint-specific Forgotten Joint Score than computer-navigated gap-balanced mechanical alignment, but the different surgical techniques and implants were bundled together so the study cannot determine whether this difference comes from the alignment strategy, technology or surgeon. The study suggests that more carefully designed research is needed to separate out which factors actually matter.

articles.title: Preoperative Opioid Use Predicts Socioeconomic Vulnerability and Worse Recovery in Elective Total Joint Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Barkus O, Zamzam M, Hodson N, Pang A, Lachman C, North WT, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip or knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: 90-day complications, length of stay, discharge destination, one-year patient-reported outcome measures, socioeconomic vulnerability
articles.take_home: Patients taking opioids before joint replacement surgery had worse outcomes, including longer hospital stays, more complications, and less functional improvement, and were also more likely to be socioeconomically vulnerable. These findings suggest that preoperative opioid use and social vulnerability are markers of higher-risk patients rather than proving that addressing these factors would improve outcomes.

articles.title: The Quality of Systematic Reviews Published in Leading Orthopaedic Surgery Journals.
articles.authors: Burger MC, van Niekerk J, Ferreira N, McCaul M
articles.study_type: Meta-epidemiological cross-sectional study assessing methodological quality
articles.population: Systematic reviews published in leading orthopaedic surgery journals
articles.sample_size: 200 systematic reviews from 1,481 screened studies, published January 2019 to December 2023
articles.outcomes: Methodological quality assessed using AMSTAR-2 tool; rates of prospective registration and use of evidence synthesis frameworks
articles.take_home: Most systematic reviews in orthopaedic surgery journals have poor methodological quality, with 91.5% rated as critically low and only 1% achieving high quality, meaning patients and doctors cannot reliably depend on these reviews to guide treatment decisions.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of the Preoperative Pan-Immune-Inflammation Value for Adverse Outcomes After Hip Arthroplasty for Femoral Neck Fracture: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Wang G, Deng X, Wang Z, Chen Z, Cao L, Su Y, et al.
articles.population: Older adults undergoing hip arthroplasty for femoral neck fracture
articles.outcomes: Postoperative intensive care unit admission (6.4%) and pulmonary infection (11.3%)
articles.take_home: A simple blood test called the pan-immune-inflammation value measured before surgery can help predict which patients are at higher risk of needing intensive care or developing chest infections after hip replacement for a broken neck of femur. Adding this test to other clinical information improved the ability to identify high-risk patients.

articles.title: Increased frequency of dislocation following total hip arthroplasty for trauma : an age- and sex-matched cohort study.
articles.authors: Williamson TR, Ali R, Kane N, Meek RMD, Jenkinson MRJ
articles.study_type: Single-centre age- and sex-matched cohort study
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty for neck of femur fracture compared with patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty for osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Primary outcome: dislocation frequency at one year. Secondary outcomes: all-cause revision, infection, periprosthetic fracture, and mortality at one year and medium-term follow-up
articles.take_home: Patients having hip replacement after a femur fracture had a four times higher risk of the hip dislocating in the first year compared to those having replacement for arthritis, even though surgeons more often used special implants designed to prevent dislocation in the fracture group. Otherwise, complication rates were similar between the two groups.

articles.title: Intra-articular knee injections in adults aged 40 to 60 years and the likelihood of progression to joint arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Panos JA, Twohey EE, Johnson SE, Boettcher BJ, Scott P, Hevesi M, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 40 to 60 years with knee osteoarthritis receiving intra-articular injections
articles.outcomes: Progression to knee joint replacement surgery (arthroplasty)
articles.take_home: Each intra-articular injection was associated with a 12% increased likelihood of eventually needing knee replacement surgery. Corticosteroid injections in patients with early osteoarthritis showed a stronger association with progression to surgery than hyaluronic acid injections.

articles.title: Routine Postoperative Radiographs Rarely Change Management After Uncomplicated Elective Hip and Knee Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Management-Change Rate and Cost.
articles.authors: Friedman A, Spicer S, Kim Y, Hill T, Kim K, McMillan S
articles.population: Adults undergoing primary elective total hip or knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Management change rate following routine postoperative radiographs; cost per management change
articles.take_home: Routine X-rays after uncomplicated hip or knee replacement surgery very rarely change how doctors treat patients, with only about 1 in 5,555 X-rays leading to a change in management. The findings suggest routine postoperative radiographs may not be necessary after straightforward elective joint replacement surgery.

articles.title: Postoperative Antibiotic Prophylaxis After Primary Total Joint Arthroplasty: Current Evidence and Future Directions.
articles.authors: Zampoli A, Verduzco Hernandez LA, Dikmen G, Parvizi J
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip and knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Optimal antibiotic prophylaxis protocols for surgical site and periprosthetic infection prevention
articles.take_home: Current guidelines disagree on whether patients need antibiotics for just before surgery, up to 24 hours after, or longer courses for high-risk patients. There is no clear consensus on the best approach, and more research is needed to identify which patients benefit from extended antibiotic coverage.

articles.title: A narrative review on the translational and clinical application of platelet-rich plasma, bone marrow concentrate and microfragmented adipose tissue for meniscal tears.
articles.authors: Pattappa G, Muller N, Zellner J, Docheva D, Angele P
articles.study_type: Narrative review of preclinical and clinical studies
articles.population: Patients with meniscal tears
articles.outcomes: Meniscal healing, pain scores (Visual Analogue Scale), knee function scores (IKDC, KOOS, Lysholm), re-rupture rates
articles.take_home: Platelet-rich plasma, bone marrow concentrate and microfragmented adipose tissue have been studied as potential treatments to help meniscal tear repair, but current evidence does not show they work better than standard surgical treatment alone. Platelet-rich plasma has been studied most, but results have been mixed.

articles.title: The impact of waiting for hip and knee arthroplasty in people of working age : an evaluation of workforce productivity effects in patients aged under 65 years.
articles.authors: Morrison SR, Lim B, Hall AJ, Clement ND, Gee C, Walmsley P
articles.population: Working-age patients aged 65 years or under undergoing primary hip or knee replacement surgery
articles.outcomes: Return to work rates, time to return to work, workplace modifications needed, preoperative work cessation, estimated productivity loss
articles.take_home: Most working-age patients (74%) returned to work after hip or knee replacement, usually within 2.5 months, though many needed workplace adjustments. Patients who stopped work before surgery were less likely to return afterwards, and longer waiting times for surgery were linked to more people stopping work preoperatively.

articles.title: Can Outpatient Total Knee Arthroplasty Be Performed at a Complex, Academic, Quaternary Referral Center?
articles.authors: Valtanen RS, Mavrommatis S, Dilger OB, Hannon CP, Bedard NA, Sierra RJ, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee replacement as outpatient (same-day discharge) at an academic hospital
articles.sample_size: 1,787 operations in 1,552 unique patients between 2019 and 2024
articles.outcomes: Emergency room visits, reoperations, revisions, and periprosthetic joint infection within 90 days of surgery
articles.take_home: Same-day discharge knee replacements can be done safely at academic hospitals, with low rates of serious complications such as infection (0.7%) and revision surgery (0.7%). However, patients made many postoperative visits (averaging nine) and 8.5% attended accident and emergency within 90 days, often for non-surgical reasons.

articles.title: Time to Minimal Clinically Important Difference After Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty: Does Patellar Resurfacing Matter?
articles.authors: Schwabe M, Singh R, Williams DL, Bono O, Bedair HS, Melnic CM
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using prospectively maintained registry
articles.population: Adults undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty with two years follow-up
articles.sample_size: 449 non-resurfaced and 1,795 resurfaced knees after propensity-score matching
articles.outcomes: Achievement of minimal clinically important difference using KOOS-PS, PROMIS Global Physical Health and PROMIS PF-10a scores; time to MCID; two-year reoperation rates
articles.take_home: Whether the kneecap surface was resurfaced during knee replacement surgery did not make a meaningful difference to how well patients recovered or how quickly they improved over two years. Non-resurfaced knees showed slightly faster improvement on one measure, but the difference was too small to matter in practice.

articles.title: Association of Preoperative Hamstring-Popliteal Angle with Postoperative Knee Extension After Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Inokuchi T, Muratsu H, Tsubosaka M, Nakano N, Kuroda R, Matsumoto T
articles.population: Patients with varus knee osteoarthritis undergoing posterior-stabilised total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Knee extension angle measured preoperatively, immediately postoperatively, at one month, and one year; association between hamstring-popliteal angle and postoperative knee extension
articles.take_home: The angle of the hamstring-popliteal muscle group before surgery was independently linked to how well the knee could straighten one year after knee replacement surgery and how much improvement occurred over time. This measurement may help predict how well patients will recover their knee extension after surgery.

articles.title: Association of Enhanced Recovery After Surgery Protocol Utilization with Postoperative Delirium in Inpatient Total Joint Arthroplasty: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Rowe JE, Giannakis P, Illescas A, Wang J, Cozowicz C, Liu J, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national database
articles.population: Adult patients undergoing elective inpatient primary total hip arthroplasty and total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Postoperative delirium during hospitalisation or within 30 days after discharge
articles.take_home: Using more enhanced recovery after surgery components was associated with a modest reduction in delirium risk after hip replacement, but not knee replacement. Delirium rates have increased over time in both procedures.

articles.title: Can All Knees Be Restored? Reproduction of Pre-Arthritic Coronal Alignment and Aseptic Revision Risk by Preoperative Phenotype: An Exploratory Stratified Competing-Risks Analysis With a Targeted Bayesian Sub-Analysis.
articles.authors: Hoskins W, Gusho CA, Rosser K, Lim M, Dunstall K
articles.study_type: Prognostic cohort study with competing-risks analysis
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee replacement
articles.outcomes: Aseptic revision rates at median 7.1 years follow-up, stratified by achievement of pre-arthritic alignment and preoperative knee phenotype
articles.take_home: Restoring the knee's pre-arthritic alignment during replacement was not significantly associated with reducing the need for revision surgery. The study suggests a possible benefit in knees that were nearly straight before arthritis, but this finding needs confirmation in other patient groups.

articles.title: Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty for Septic Versus Aseptic Loosening: A Minimum 20-Year Comparative Study of Survivorship, Functional Outcomes, and Failure Predictors.
articles.authors: Kim YH, Park JW
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision total knee arthroplasty for septic or aseptic loosening
articles.outcomes: Knee Society Scores, implant survivorship at 25 years, re-revision rates, reinfection rates, and predictors of failure
articles.take_home: Both septic and aseptic revision knee replacements provided long-term improvements, but revision for infected loosening resulted in worse functional scores, higher re-revision rates (25.3% versus 11.4%), more reinfections, and lower implant survival at 25 years (74.7% versus 88.6%) compared to aseptic loosening.

articles.title: The Prognostic Implication of Preoperative Troponin Elevation at Hospital Admission in Hip Fracture Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Baldy de Sousa F, Pasqualotto E, Pasqualotto T, Martins EC, de Almeida Osterne F, Baldy Dos Reis F
articles.population: Hip fracture patients at hospital admission
articles.outcomes: Overall mortality, one-month mortality, three-month mortality, arrhythmia, congestive heart failure, length of hospital stay
articles.take_home: Patients with raised troponin (a heart enzyme) at hospital admission had more than double the risk of death compared to those with normal troponin levels. This effect was strongest in the first month after admission, suggesting troponin levels could help identify high-risk hip fracture patients early on.

articles.title: Total Hip Arthroplasty versus Hemiarthroplasty for Displaced Fragility Femoral Neck Fractures in Older Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Mortality, Reoperation, and Surgical Complications.
articles.authors: Pierce TP, Badawi JM, Alhammadi H, Sabti AA, Alsaleh N, Al-Hadhrami MS, et al.
articles.population: Older adults with displaced fragility femoral neck fractures treated surgically
articles.sample_size: 114,064 total hip arthroplasties and 443,016 hemiarthroplasties from 31 studies
articles.outcomes: Mortality at one month and one year, revision surgery, instability, periprosthetic joint infection, and periprosthetic fractures
articles.take_home: Total hip arthroplasty was associated with lower one-year death rates compared to hemiarthroplasty, but patients who had total hip arthroplasty had a higher risk of hip instability in the long term. No clear differences were found between the two procedures for other complications.

articles.title: Correcting to Neutral in Severely Deformed Total Knee Arthroplasty Is Associated With Reduced Aseptic Loosening and Instability.
articles.authors: Hoskins W, Gusho CA, Rosser K, Lim M, Dunstall K, Vince KG
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty with severe coronal deformity
articles.outcomes: Aseptic revision rates; incidence of revision for loosening or instability at 5 years
articles.take_home: Correcting the knee alignment towards neutral during total knee replacement in severely deformed knees reduces the risk of aseptic loosening and instability compared with preserving the original deformity. Adding stems or constraint options did not improve outcomes, so alignment correction alone was most important.

articles.title: Combined Coronal and Rotational Malalignment Is an Independent Predictor of Survivorship After Total Knee Arthroplasty: Results at a Mean Follow-up of 20.5 Years.
articles.authors: Kim YH, Park JW
articles.population: Patients who had primary total knee replacement
articles.sample_size: 650 patients (1,140 knees) followed for mean of 20.5 years
articles.outcomes: Aseptic revision rates and implant survivorship at 20.5 years, stratified by coronal and rotational alignment
articles.take_home: When both the coronal and rotational alignment of a knee replacement are out of target, the implant is significantly more likely to need revision surgery. Having only coronal misalignment alone did not increase revision risk, but rotational misalignment alone or combined misalignment both did.

articles.title: Comparison of computed tomography-based tibial torsion measurement techniques reveals significant technique-dependent differences.
articles.authors: Benefelds M, Juen U, Kaiser P, Lindtner R, Kummann M, Mayr R
articles.population: Adult patients
articles.outcomes: Tibial torsion measurements using six different CT-based techniques; intra- and interobserver reliability assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients
articles.take_home: Different CT measurement techniques produce significantly different tibial torsion values, with the Jend axis method giving substantially higher readings than other methods. Clinicians need to know which measurement technique was used when interpreting results, as the choice of technique substantially affects the numerical value obtained.

articles.title: Retatrutide Once Weekly in Adults with Knee Osteoarthritis Pain and Obesity.
articles.authors: Schnitzer TJ, Hunter DJ, Conaghan PG, Sharma AM, Pedersen SD, Chen K, et al.
articles.study_type: Phase 3 randomised controlled trials (two trials: TRIUMPH-4 and TRIUMPH-1-OA)
articles.population: Adults without diabetes who had painful knee osteoarthritis and a body mass index of at least 27
articles.sample_size: 445 participants in TRIUMPH-4 and 574 in TRIUMPH-1-OA
articles.outcomes: Change in WOMAC pain score (range 0 to 10) and percent change in body weight. TRIUMPH-4 at 68 weeks: retatrutide 9 mg reduced pain by 3.96 points and 12 mg by 3.74 points compared to placebo's 2.12 points; body weight reduction of 20.0% (9 mg) and 23.7% (12 mg) versus 4.6% with placebo. TRIUMPH-1-OA at 80 weeks: retatrutide doses of 4, 9, and 12 mg reduced pain by 3.22, 3.48, and 3.64 points respectively compared to placebo's 1.87 points. Serious adverse events were more common with retatrutide; most common adverse events were gastrointestinal.
articles.take_home: Retatrutide, a weekly injection, reduced knee osteoarthritis pain and body weight more than placebo in people with obesity. However, it caused more serious side effects and common stomach problems compared to placebo.
